t: Minimum Space Wasted From Packaging — One Supplier, Prefix Sums, Upper Bounds
o: Choose exactly one supplier; every package must go into a box at least its size, and the waste is the unused box space summed over all packages. Example 1: packages [2,3,5] with supplier boxes [4,8] waste (4-2) + (4-3) + (8-5) = 6, while the alternative supplier [2,8] does worse, so 6 is the answer. Example 2 returns -1 outright: no supplier owns any box fitting the size-5 package. Example 3 shows the aggregation idea: sorting supplier [10,5,14] to 5,10,14 serves the sorted packages in three contiguous chunks totaling waste 9. With up to 10^5 packages and 10^5 total boxes of sizes up to 10^5, per-supplier evaluation must be near-linear after sorting, and totals reach ~10^10 — so accumulate in 64-bit and apply the 10^9+7 modulo only once at the end.
k: Each package independently wants its supplier's smallest adequate box, so with both sides sorted the assignment becomes contiguous ranges of packages per box size.
Prefix sums over sorted packages give any range's size total in O(1), making each box a single upper_bound query.
A supplier qualifies if and only if its largest box fits the largest package.

a.i: For each supplier, sort its boxes, reject it if the biggest box cannot hold the biggest package, then for every package binary-search the smallest fitting box and add box - package to the waste. A direct transcription of the rules: correct and easy to defend, but it pays one binary search per package per supplier.
s: Per supplier: sort its boxes; skip the supplier entirely if max box < max package.
For each package, binary-search the first fitting box and add its size minus the package size.
Keep the best supplier total; output it modulo 10^9+7, or -1 if every supplier was rejected.
a.t: O(K log K + m * n log K) — each supplier sorts its K_j boxes then probes all n packages by binary search (K = total boxes).

a.n: Approach 2: Prefix Sums with Range Aggregation
a.i: With packages sorted, one box size b covers a contiguous chunk: every package in (previous bound, b]. Precompute prefix sums so each chunk's package total costs O(1); then each box is one upper_bound plus one arithmetic expression: b * count - rangeSum. Per-supplier work collapses from n searches to B searches over boxes only — a decisive win when n is large and many packages share box sizes.
s: Sort packages once; build prefix sums pre where pre[i] is the sum of the first i packages.
Per supplier: sort its boxes; reject it if its largest box is below the largest package.
Walk boxes ascending: hi = upper_bound(packages, b, lo); add b * (hi - lo) - (pre[hi] - pre[lo]); set lo = hi.
Stop early once lo reaches n; track the minimum waste across suppliers.
Return best % (10^9+7), or -1 if no supplier qualified.

c.python:
class Solution:
    def minWastedSpace(self, packages: List[int], boxes: List[List[int]]) -> int:
        from bisect import bisect_right
        packages.sort()
        n = len(packages)
        pre = [0] * (n + 1)
        for i, p in enumerate(packages):
            pre[i + 1] = pre[i] + p
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        best = inf
        for box in boxes:
            box.sort()
            if box[-1] < packages[-1]:
                continue
            wasted = 0
            lo = 0
            for b in box:
                hi = bisect_right(packages, b, lo)
                wasted += b * (hi - lo) - (pre[hi] - pre[lo])
                lo = hi
                if lo == n:
                    break
            best = min(best, wasted)
        return best % MOD if best < inf else -1

a.t: O(n log n + K log K + K log n) — sorting packages once; each of the K boxes then costs an amortized scan step plus one upper_bound.

w: Use Approach 1 to explain why ranges suffice, then implement the prefix-sum version. Pitfalls: each supplier's box list arrives unsorted (sort before scanning), keep totals in 64-bit and apply the modulo exactly once at the end, and never forget the -1 case when even the largest package has no home. Follow-ups: mixing suppliers per package (take the globally cheapest fitting box per package), or handling streamed packages online.
